title: Tighten a tourniquet's windlass to the green and lock it
instruction: Tighten the tourniquet on the training leg until its gauge reads green, then lock the rod in its clip.
context: Uncontrolled bleeding from a limb is a leading cause of preventable death after injury. A windlass tourniquet stops it: twist the rod until the bleeding stops, then lock it in the tourniquet's clip, as armies, ambulance services and Stop the Bleed courses teach. Robots sent to mass-casualty scenes or places medics can't reach would need it too. A gauge stands in for the bleeding; the band pulls the rod back whenever nothing holds it, and the clip lines up twice before the gauge is green.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. A training thigh (firm skin-toned foam cylinder, 12.7 cm across, 40 cm long) lies along y, axis at x 28 and 6.55 cm up, hip end on the robot's left, held down by a webbing strap over it at each end onto two pairs of wooden chocks (3 x 4 x 3.5 cm tall) at y +-15, inner faces 5.6 cm either side of the axis. A C-A-T Gen 7 windlass tourniquet (unmodified blue trainer, NSN 6910-01-560-2972: band 3.8 cm wide, ribbed rod about 15 cm long and 12 mm across, its own windlass clip) is round it at y 0, fastened snug, its free end stuck back along the band and taped flat (nothing loose to pull) and its time strap folded flat away from the clip, over a 5 x 42 cm air bladder (heat-sealed TPU-coated nylon) wrapped once round the thigh with 2 cm of overlap, pumped to 60 mmHg before the trial, then sealed: the pump bulb is taken off and the port capped. Its 5 mm rubber tube comes out under the band on the knee side, below the thigh, and runs along the table to the gauge's post. The windlass sits on top, the rod's axis 14.85 cm up. The clip is on the band beside it, toward the arms: its two C-shaped hooks sit at the band's edges, about 4.3 cm toward the arms from the windlass and 1.9 cm either side of the band's centre line, so a locked rod lies along the band about 24 degrees to one side, its end tipped about 21 degrees down into a hook. The rod starts level, 30 degrees clockwise (seen from above) from where an end lines up with the hip-side hook: one end toward the arms and the hip, 54 degrees off the band's line. An aneroid gauge (12 cm dial, 0 to 300 mmHg, green tape on the dial from 250, stop at 300) stands on a 14 mm square post and 7 x 7 cm foot at x 43, y -15, dial centre 12 cm up, tilted 50 degrees up toward the arms. Both arms start at the ready pose with open grippers.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial from a photo of the gauge and the clip, and the video. Locked: an end of the rod snapped down past a hook's lips (after the trial, a light upward pull on that end by hand doesn't free it). Green: the gauge at 250 mmHg or more with no part of the robot touching the band, bladder, thigh or gauge. Take the first line that applies. 1.0 (success, ends the trial): for the whole last 1 s, green, rod locked, and no part of the robot within 1 cm of the rod or clip. 0.5: green with the rod locked, or held (part of the robot within 1 cm of the rod) within 5 degrees of level, not pressed down onto the band. 0.25: rod locked, not green, wherever the robot is. 0: anything else, including letting go unlocked.
reset_notes: Lift the rod out of the clip, untwist it to its start (level, one end toward the arms and the hip, 30 degrees clockwise from lining up with the hip-side hook), and check the gauge reads 60 mmHg (re-pump through the port if not). Every 10 trials, re-check the gauge at the 30, 78 and 210 degree hook positions.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. Thigh, band, clip and gauge are fixed; the rod turns about the vertical and tips up to 30 degrees on a 0.3 N m/rad spring. Hooks' floors, walls and lead-ins collide; the lips are drawn only, and task code holds a seated rod down. The band's pull, 0.06 N m/rad (0.22 N m in the green), is assumed, not measured: a real C-A-T likely pulls harder. Gauge: 60 mmHg plus 1 per degree. Snap force and the strap aren't modelled.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (its hands reached the rod and turned it at most 17 degrees, raising the gauge to 77 mmHg, but it never locked it); demo: 1.0
